title: Mexican Tomatillo-Poblano Salsa Verde
description: Gently simmered tomatillos and roasted mild poblano blend into a thick green table sauce brightened with cilantro.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: fresh tomatillos
ingredients.note: Weight after removing husks, rinsing and quartering.

ingredients.name: plain cooked mild poblano pepper
ingredients.note: Mild home-roasted pepper, peeled and seeded.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: table salt
ingredients.note: Fine table salt, about 590 mg sodium per 1/4 teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/16 tsp total.

steps.title: Soften the tomatillos
steps.text: Simmer {tom}, {ga} and {w} under a lid for 7–9 minutes until the tomatillos lose their bright green color and break under a spoon.

steps.title: Blend the salsa
steps.text: Take off the heat and blend the cooked base with {pob}, {cil}, {lj} and {salt} until smooth.

steps.title: Set the body
steps.text: Return the salsa to low heat and cook uncovered for 2–4 minutes until it coats a spoon without a watery rim.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Serve warm over soft chicken enchiladas or eggs, or cool and use as a table sauce.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/16 tsp table salt in place of 1/4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit the lime and replace half the tomatillos by weight with cooked peeled zucchini. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 19 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 3.7 g total carbohydrate, 0.4 g fat, 1.0 g fiber, 149 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 19 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 3.7 g total carbohydrate, 0.4 g fat, 1.0 g fiber, 38 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
